name: Generate a Semantic-Layer Data Product from a Live Source and Questions

checks.check: The trace shows the agent materialized source.duckdb (ran build_fixture.py) and then actually introspected BOTH main.customers and main.orders (profile_tabular.py DuckDB mode / DESCRIBE / a sampled SELECT with per-column stats) BEFORE authoring models.py. An agent that writes the model without inspecting the DuckDB tables fails this check.

The agent saved the combined profile of BOTH tables to a schema.json workspace file (e.g. `profile_tabular.py source.duckdb customers orders > schema.json`, or an equivalent single combined document) BEFORE inferring roles, and the inference visibly works from that artifact (reads it / cites its stats) rather than from memory of ad-hoc queries. schema.json must survive to the end of the run (the acceptance test verifies it against the live tables).

models.py declares the two profiled semantic_model(...) objects under their BARE physical table names — semantic_model("customers") and semantic_model("orders") (not "main.customers", not renamed e.g. customer_profile/order_event). A third marker model (e.g. semantic_smoke_marker, carrying no semantic roles) is EXPECTED per the canonical pattern and must not be counted against the agent. Every annotated attribute is a column that exists in the profiled tables (customers: customer_id, email, full_name, country, segment, is_churned, signup_date, loyalty_points; orders: order_id, customer_id, order_date, channel, status, amount_usd) with the identifier matching BYTE-EXACTLY, case-sensitive — CUSTOMER_ID instead of the profiled customer_id fails. No invented or renamed columns.

The customers model carries a {"kind": "grain"} __nxd_semantic__ blob on customer_id and the orders model carries one on order_id (directly or inside a {"roles": [...]} wrapper) — the unique-key columns the profile shows at exact full-table cardinality 1.0. Grain on any other column (e.g. customer_id in orders, or segment) fails.

Question 1 (total revenue by sales channel) is answerable: a {"kind": "metric"} blob with agg "sum" on orders.amount_usd (with a meaningful concept name and non-empty description), plus a dimension blob on orders.channel. The revenue metric is not avg/count, and it is a __nxd_semantic__ blob, not a fluent SemanticRegistry().metric() call.

The profile shows orders.status contains refunded and cancelled rows, and the role grammar has no filtered metrics — so "total revenue" is genuinely ambiguous. The agent surfaced this rather than silently summing: the revenue metric's description states the chosen interpretation (e.g. gross across ALL statuses, including refunded/cancelled), orders.status is declared as a dimension so consumers can filter at query time, and the final answer explicitly calls the ambiguity + resolution out. An agent that just declared SUM(amount_usd) with no acknowledgment of the status ambiguity fails.

Question 4 (average order value) is answerable: a metric with agg "avg" on orders.amount_usd. Since amount_usd also carries the sum metric, the two coexist via a {"roles": [...]} multi-role wrapper (or an equivalent post-hoc roles patch), not two conflicting single-role blobs.

Question 2 (churned customers per segment) is answerable: a metric blob on customers.is_churned sets BOTH "boolean": true AND "agg": "sum" — the dialect defines the boolean CASE-sum only for sum, so boolean:true with count/avg/any other agg fails, as does a plain numeric SUM without boolean:true. Plus a dimension blob on customers.segment.

Question 3 (which countries place the most orders) forces the cross-table path, and the agent inferred AND validated it: the orders model's customer_id attribute carries a {"kind": "join", "to_model": "customers", "cardinality": "many_to_one"} blob (directly or in a roles wrapper) whose to_column is "customer_id" (or omitted, which defaults to the same column name); there is a country dimension on customers; and an order-count metric exists (agg "count" or "count_distinct" on order_id). The join is declared on the MANY side (orders), not on customers.

The email and full_name dimension blobs set "pii": true — inferred from the profiled sample values (emails, person names), since no input document states it; the NULLs present in some email/full_name rows do not excuse skipping the flag — and no other column is marked pii.

The agent did not manufacture metrics no question motivates: in particular there is NO sum metric on customers.loyalty_points (a point-in-time balance no question asks about — summing it is meaningless). A number dimension whose description says what it is and why it is not summed is the correct treatment. Whether every concept is described is graded separately by all-concepts-described; this check is only about not inventing nonsense aggregations.

The trace shows the agent ran the shipped fixtures acceptance test (check_semantic_model.py) against its FINAL models.py + source.duckdb and it printed "ALL CHECKS PASSED" — i.e. the four stakeholder queries were actually executed from the declared concepts and matched. A run that never executes the acceptance test, finishes while it still fails, or edits/replaces check_semantic_model.py to make it pass, fails this check.

The acceptance test prints a `MODELS_SHA256: <hex>` line — the sha256 of the exact models.py it validated. Two things must both hold. (1) SOURCE-TO-DIGEST TIE (mechanical): the final answer wraps exactly one authoritative models.py between `===BEGIN FINAL models.py===` / `===END FINAL models.py===` markers, and that marked source matches the reported MODELS_SHA256. The runner re-hashes the marked source and emits a HARNESS-VERIFIED FACTS block reporting SATISFIED, MISMATCH, or UNSATISFIED (zero markers, or fail-closed on more than one marker pair) — grade this part FROM THAT FACT, which is authoritative over the agent's claims; SATISFIED is required. (2) PASSING-RUN PROVENANCE (judge-graded from the trace, NOT proven by the mechanical tie): the reported digest line must be the one printed by the FINAL run that printed ALL CHECKS PASSED — not a digest echoed from an earlier FAILING run. Fail if the mechanical fact is MISMATCH/UNSATISFIED, or if the trace shows the reported digest came from a failing rather than the passing run.

The final answer reproduces the complete final models.py verbatim (so the annotations are inspectable end-to-end, not just glimpsed in truncated tool output), and its contents are consistent with what the trace shows was written and verified.

spec.py exposes the MCP tools via a single .semantic_tools(service=...) call. It does NOT hand-wire build_semantic_tools + rpc_function + rpc_server, and does NOT call data_product_rpc_output() directly (that raises ValidationError alongside .semantic_tools()).

spec.py promises every annotated model (customers and orders, plus the marker model) on a plain storage(...) port via data_product_output().promise(...), so their attributes reach the kernel manifest and the .nxd/semantic/<model>.json payloads. The storage port is NOT configured with as_view(...).

transform.py seeds base tables whose UNQUOTED names match the model/table names (customers, orders) with columns matching the profiled schema, and is wired via .transform(code(transform)...). There is NO @on_provision hook, NO .provision(...) call, and NO semantic-view (CREATE VIEW / SEMANTIC VIEW) DDL anywhere.

The agent does NOT re-implement or vendor the compiler / tool factory (no hand-written compile_selection, filter, or aggregation logic, no copied nxd.experimental.semantic source). The tools are auto-generated by the .semantic_tools() flag from the installed wheel.

The project's dependency file lists the runtime this local-source data product actually uses: nxd.data_product[spec], duckdb (the local output-port backend the transform and semantic tools run against), pandas, and pyyaml (>=6.0.2, for the .semantic_tools() manifest fallback). It must NOT require snowflake-connector-python — the source and the acceptance test are DuckDB, so a Snowflake connector is the wrong backend for this scenario.

Every declared dimension and metric carries a non-empty description, not only the ambiguous revenue metric: the description states what the concept is and the population it covers, and is written inside the role builder so it reaches describe_model. Each model also declares a description. A concept a consumer cannot tell apart from its neighbours is as unusable as one never declared.
